bioghist.head: Historical Information
bioghist.p: Context for Records:The treasurer is one of the five constitutional officers outlined in the Virginia Constitution. The Constitution of 1869 placed the sheriff's tax collection function in the new office of treasurer, who was both the cashier and the bookkeeper of the county. During the township period (1870-1875) the township collector and clerk also had treasurer's functions; later the county treasurer's duties were expanded to include the township officer's activities.

Locality History: Mathews County was named for Thomas Mathews, of Norfolk, the Speaker of the Virginia House of Delegates when it was formed from Gloucester County by a statute passed on 16 December 1790 to take effect on 1 May 1791.
Locality History: p>Lost Locality Note:Most Mathews County records were burned in Richmond on 3 April 1865, where they had been moved for safekeeping during the Civil War.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Mathews County (Va.) Treasurer Records, 1870-1963, consist of Treasurer's settlements, reports on audits, operating funds information, and correspondence.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p:
For descriptive purposes, the collection has been divided into two series:
Series I: Processed Treasurer Records, 1874, 1886-1895
Series II: Unprocessed Treasurer Records, 1870-1963

relatedmaterial.head: Related Material
relatedmaterial.p: Additional Mathews County Records can be found on microfilm at the Library of Virginia. Consult "A Guide to Virginia County and City Records on Microfilm."
